clue.text: Person who's picky, upset and in a bad mood

indicators.note: in says one piece sits inside the other, here the reworked word inside the mood

parts.note: a pet is a fit of sulking, as in 'in a pet'

indicators.note: upset says the letters of the small word and are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fussy who is also upset and sulking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like part of the picky person's mood, but it shuffles the little word 'and' to DAN; 'in' sets that inside a sulk, as in the British phrase 'in a pet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedant fusses over small details of rules and correctness, so is a picky person.

clue.text: Illustrations describing one exercise programme

indicators.note: describing in its sense of drawing round, so the pictures enclose the numeral

parts.note: plates are full-page illustrations in a book
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Pictures showing a workout routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing a line round, so PLATES goes around I.
explanation.definitionFit: Pilates is a system of exercises for core strength and flexibility.

clue.text: Karate expert from Berlin threatening opponent

parts.note: a dan is a black-belt grade in martial arts, hence an expert
someone from Berlin is German

explanation.surface: A karate black belt from Berlin is a menacing foe.
explanation.definitionFit: A danger man is a dangerous adversary, one posing a threat.

clue.text: No quote stands up as purely intellectual

indicators.note: stands up in a down answer means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to quote

explanation.surface: Without a quotation, this stands as pure thought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stands up' turns CITE into ETIC in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Noetic relates to the mind and intellect alone, from the Greek for thought.

clue.text: Legal meetings cut short and since disbanded

indicators.note: cut short says the word for meetings loses its final letter

parts.note: fora is a plural of forum, a meeting place for discussion

indicators.note: disbanded says the letters of since are broken up and regrouped

explanation.surface: Legal gatherings were trimmed and have since been wound up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut short' trims FORA to FOR; 'disbanded' rearranges SINCE into ENSIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic science and evidence serve the courts, so the word means relating to law.

clue.text: Killer sea creature minutes away from Spanish island

indicators.note: away from says the short time unit is taken off the island's name

parts.note: Minorca is one of Spain's Balearic Islands
min is the abbreviation for minutes

explanation.surface: A deadly marine animal is a few minutes from a Spanish island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away from' removes MIN from MINORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The orca is also called the killer whale, a predator of the oceans.

clue.text: Smell said to rival strong spirit

indicators.note: said says the word for smell is heard, not spelt

parts.note: an odour is a smell; spoken, it can pass for the French eau de
to vie is to compete with, to rival

explanation.surface: A spirit is said to compete with a powerful smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' sounds ODOUR as EAU DE; VIE then follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de vie, French for water of life, is a strong colourless fruit brandy.

clue.text: Nothing but sandwiches and white wine

indicators.note: sandwiches says the first word encloses the letter for nothing

parts.note: save, as in all save one, means but or except
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Nothing but sandwiches and a glass of white.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sandwiches' puts O inside SAVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Soave is a dry white wine from the Veneto in Italy.

clue.text: Having stomach issues caused by fizzy cola and ice

indicators.note: fizzy says the letters of cola and ice bubble up into a new order

explanation.surface: Tummy trouble brought on by fizzy cola and ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fizzy' rearranges COLAICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Coeliac disease is a gluten intolerance that damages the gut, causing digestive problems.

clue.text: Underwear that is going to stay on

indicators.note: going says the letters for that is leave the longer word

parts.note: lingerie is women's underwear
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Underwear that will be kept on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going' removes IE from LINGERIE.
explanation.definitionFit: To linger is to remain somewhere longer than needed, staying on.

clue.text: Copper breaks into a clapped-out car with precision

indicators.note: breaks into says the metal's symbol forces its way inside the old car

parts.note: a crate is slang for a battered old car
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer breaks into an old banger, and does it precisely.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper looks like a policeman but is the chemical symbol CU, put inside CRATE after A.
explanation.definitionFit: Accurate describes something done exactly right, so it serves as 'with precision'.

clue.text: Laid on the floor and prepared to drink

parts.note: set means ready or prepared
to down a drink is to swallow it in one

explanation.surface: Collapsed on the floor and ready for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something down is to put it on the ground, laying it there.

clue.text: It is recalled in essays and a paper

indicators.note: in says the turned word sits inside the essays

parts.note: themes are school essays or compositions

indicators.note: recalled read as called back, so the word it is turned back to front

explanation.surface: Something remembered appears in essays and in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is recalled' reads as 'is called back', turning IT into TI; 'in' places it among the essays. 'and' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: The Times is a long-established British daily newspaper.

clue.text: Enemy destroyed island from a peninsula

indicators.note: destroyed says the letters of enemy are wrecked and reassembled

explanation.surface: A foe has wiped out an island off a peninsula.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destroyed' rearranges ENEMY into YEMEN, then I is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen lies at the southern end of the Arabian Peninsula, so something Yemeni comes from there.

clue.text: Blonde perm perhaps somehow initially seems straight to me

parts.note: fair hair is blonde
a perm is an example of a hairdo, or do

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A blonde perm somehow looks straight to me.
explanation.walkthrough: FAIR DOS is a British exclamation meaning that's fair, that's a square deal.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying fair dos concedes that something is honest and even-handed, as straight dealing seems to the speaker.

clue.text: Almost the final house?

definitions.meaning: a ... is a ...-final, the round just before the final
a ... is a ...-detached house, sharing one wall with its neighbour

explanation.surface: Is this nearly the last house?
explanation.definitionFit: Semi is short both for a semi-final and for a semi-detached house, a common British home type.

clue.text: I get bogged down endlessly after I do business, and it's impractical

indicators.note: after says the first part of the clue comes behind the second in the answer

parts.note: to deal is to trade or do business

indicators.note: endlessly says the word for getting bogged down loses its last letter

parts.note: to stick is to get stuck or bogged down

explanation.surface: Someone who gets mired after doing deals is unrealistic.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue's two halves swap places: 'after' puts the I who gets bogged down behind the I who does business, and 'endlessly' drops the last letter of the sticking word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idealistic person pursues perfect principles over workable plans, so is impractical.

clue.text: Got up and went to an event

explanation.surface: Dressed and showed up at a function.
explanation.definitionFit: Being turned out describes how someone is dressed, and turning out means attending in numbers.

clue.text: Professional journalist from Central Europe?

parts.note: someone from Poland in Central Europe is Polish
ed is the short form of editor, a journalist

explanation.surface: A capable reporter from Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: A polished performance is refined and expert, the mark of a professional.

clue.text: No RAM was reconfigured as regards demanding programmes?

indicators.note: reconfigured suits the computing surface and says the letters are rearranged

parts.note: re means about or as regards

explanation.surface: A computer with no memory was reset for programs that ask a lot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reconfigured' rearranges NO RAM WAS into RANSOMWA. The question mark flags that 'demanding' is literal: these programs demand a ransom.
explanation.definitionFit: Ransomware is malicious software that locks files and demands payment, so its programs literally make demands.

clue.text: Certain type of gem Sue uncovered

indicators.note: uncovered says the word for sue loses its outer letters

parts.note: to sue is to take legal action, to prosecute

explanation.surface: Sue has unwrapped a particular precious stone.
explanation.walkthrough: Sue looks like a name but is the verb, PROSECUTE, which 'uncovered' strips to ROSECUT.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose cut is a style of gem cutting with a flat base and triangular facets, so it names a type of gem.

clue.text: Some off-colour, dull khaki comes from here

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Some drab, dull khaki colour comes from here.
explanation.definitionFit: Khaki is a loanword from the language of Pakistan and north India, meaning dust-coloured.

clue.text: Try to forget about leaving vague information at the end

indicators.note: leaving says the letter for about departs from the word for vague

parts.note: unclear means vague
C is short for circa, about

indicators.note: at the end points to the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Seeking to forget vague details at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' takes C out of UNCLEAR to give UNLEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: To unlearn is to deliberately discard knowledge or a habit from one's mind.

clue.text: Reference book gets bought, finally. Finally!

parts.note: an atlas is a book of maps used for reference

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Someone finally buys a reference book, to their relief.
explanation.definitionFit: At last is an exclamation of relief when something long awaited happens.

clue.text: Small, well-known Austrian bread product

parts.note: Arnie is Arnold Schwarzenegger, the Austrian-born actor

explanation.surface: A small, famous Austrian baked good.
explanation.walkthrough: A SARNIE is British slang for a sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A sarnie is made with slices of bread, so it is a bread product.

clue.text: Scoundrel downing good Beaujolais?

indicators.note: downing says the letter for good is moved further down this down answer

parts.note: a rogue is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A rascal knocking back a fine red wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Downing looks like drinking, but it moves G lower in ROGUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Rouge is French for red, and Beaujolais is a red wine, an example of vin rouge.

clue.text: Vehicle's part for which you need to pay, very possibly

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay it
well, as in 'may well', means very possibly

explanation.surface: A car component you will probably have to pay for.
explanation.walkthrough: Foot means pay, as in foot the bill; well means very possibly, as in 'it may well'.
explanation.definitionFit: A footwell is the space for the feet in front of a car's seats, part of the vehicle.

clue.text: Head bishop ousted? Not again!

indicators.note: ousted says the letter for bishop is thrown out of the word for head

parts.note: bonce is British slang for the head
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: The chief bishop thrown out yet again?
explanation.walkthrough: BONCE is British slang for the head; 'ousted' removes B.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done once happens a single time and is not repeated.

clue.text: Caught speeding? That's devastating!

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
rushing means going fast, speeding

explanation.surface: Getting nicked for speeding is a disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A crushing blow or defeat is overwhelming, so crushing means devastating.

clue.text: To kick off with, paneer and kofta. Alternatively, a …

definitions.text: To kick off with, paneer and kofta. Alternatively, a …

indicators.note: to kick off with points to the starting letters of the next three words

parts.note: or is the word for alternatively

explanation.surface: A menu of Indian starters: paneer and kofta, or else a pakora.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the ellipsis invites the answer as one more starter option.
explanation.definitionFit: A pakora is a fried Indian snack served as a starter alongside paneer and kofta.

clue.text: Butt piercing annoys hipsters

indicators.note: piercing says the word for butt goes through the middle of the other

parts.note: tries, as in tries one's patience, means annoys
the butt is the end of something

explanation.surface: A pierced bottom irritates the fashionable crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butt' suggests a backside, but it means an end, as in a cigarette butt; 'piercing' runs it through the word for annoys.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendies are people who follow the latest fashions, much like hipsters.

clue.text: Heart medication immediately starts to induce nausea

parts.note: stat is medical shorthand for immediately

indicators.note: starts to points to the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A cardiac drug quickly makes you feel sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Statins lower cholesterol to protect against heart disease, a common cardiac drug.
